occurrences.text: CoreLink is fundamentally ONE multi-tenant content-addressable store (R2 + D1 + the 2-level "moat") fronted by MANY native client cache protocols, so a customer points an existing tool's flag (`--remote_cache=`, `TURBO_API=`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` WebDAV, `docker push`, `~/.cargo`) at CoreLink and gets faster + cheaper CI with zero proprietary client. Surfaces actually wired + mounted in the container (crates/corelink-container/src/routes.rs:545-676): native CAS (`/v1/cas`, BLAKE3) and AC (`/v1/ac`), Bazel REAPI v2 REST bridge (`/bazel/v2`, SHA-256), Turborepo v8 (`/v8/artifacts`, opaque hash), OCI Distribution v1.1 registry (`/v2` + `/token`, sha256 digest mapped to BLAKE3 in the moat), and the cargo/sccache (`/cargo`, HTTP/WebDAV), Homebrew (`/brew`), npm (`/npm`), and PyPI/pip (`/pip`) read-through caches. All write surfaces share ONE storage chokepoint with identical tenant-isolation, scope, native-PAT-possession, $-ceiling and byte-accounting gates, plus per-tenant pre-body concurrency caps. The digest scheme forks per surface (BLAKE3 native/sccache, SHA-256 Bazel) but every keyspace single-functions under a per-tenant R2 prefix. A second full gRPC REAPI implementation (corelink-reapi: BatchUpdateBlobs / Capabilities / ByteStream) exists but is NOT mounted in the container (near-ready). The cross-tenant network-effect moat is real for PUBLIC content (brew/pip wheels) but partial for npm tarballs (per-tenant for now).
